condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

Project objective: Improved waste management practices in towns and municipalities through the introduction of integrated wastewater treatment plants and biogas digester.

Result 1.1: National Solid Waste Management Policy was revised to include waste to energy aspects. Result 1.2: At least 15 technical personnel and champions from the four pilot cities of Jinja, Masaka, Mbale and Mbarara were sensitized on integrated waste management approaches through visiting successful cases/sites in KCCA and NWSC. Result 1.3 Waste management plans and waste management ordinances for the Cities of Arua, Hoima, Soroti, Gulu, Lira,Fortportal and Municipalities of Tororo, Masindi, Kabale were reviewed. Data was obtained for computation of standard baselines from stakeholders i.e sugarcane factories and NWSC on the Municipal wastewater plants

Project objective: Improved waste management practices in towns and municipalities through the introduction of integrated wastewater treatment plants and biogas digesters.
1. Twelve thousand two hundred (12,200) tonnes CO2eq/yr. (0.4MW of electricity is currently produced from the Kakira Sugar Limited plant).
2: One thousand five (1,005); (674 male and 331 female) have directly benefited while, an estimated five million five hundred (5,000,500) people have been reached indirectly through the awareness and sensitization drives carried out by the project using various media platforms.
3: A total of Nineteen million six hundred fourty six thousand five hundred fifty seven USD dollars (US$19,646,557) has been mobilized as equity for construction of Kakira Sugar Limited ($4million) and NWSC ($15,646,557) biogas plants which are now operational. 4: 2,800 MWh/yr from the 0.4 MW biogas plant at Kakira Sugar Limited.
Results attained under Component 1: Establishing enabling market conditions, institutional strengthening and capacity building for improved waste management and promotion of MSW-based biogas systems.
1.1 Five (5) draft policy/ ordinances have been developed for the cities of Mbale, Mbarara, Masaka and Jinja pending clearance by the solicitor.
1.2 A total of nineteen (19) urban areas i.e. 11 cities of Jinja, Masaka, Mbale, Kampala, Soroti, Fort Portal, Lira, Gulu, Arua, Hoima and 3 municipalities of Tororo, Masindi, Kabale plus 5 in the Greater Kampala Metropolitan Area(GKMA) of Nansana, Mukono, Makindye, Kira and Entebbe are reporting on IWM approaches promoted by the project.
1.3 Two (2) Multi-stakeholder platforms have now been formed by the project – National multi-stakeholders’ platform and GKMA- Greater Kampala Metropolitan Area Technical Working Group.
Results attained under Component 2: Demonstration and investment in integrated wastewater treatment and biogas plants
2.1: 0.8MW installed. 0.4MW from Kakira Sugar Works is already being fed into the national grid. Also, 0.4 MW NWSC biogas plant is operational although not feeding electricity into the grid.
2.2: Two (2) investments, i.e. Kakira Sugar Limited biogas plant, and NWSC biogas Plant in Kampala are already in place as demonstration plants.
Results attained under Component 3: Scale up the use of biogas technologies in other municipalities
3.1 Utilized seed funds from GEF grant to carry out feasibility studies to establish biogas to electricity plant in KCCA and enhance biogas production in NWSC plant.
3.2 Currently, one project concept for a waste to electricity plant installation at KCCA with possibility of scale up to the other cities of Mbale, Masaka, Mbarara and Jinja has been submitted to the Program preparations committee of the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development pending further review by the Ministry of Finance
3.3 About Two Hundred thirty nine thousand eight hundred twenty five US Dollars (USD 239,825) of the seed grant from GEF/UNDP has been disbursed for feasibility studies carried out for KCCA and NWSC as well as characterization and waste flow studies for Mbarara and Mbale Cities
Results attained under component 4: Knowledge Management and Monitoring and Evaluation
4.1 The project launched a website in November 2020 and it is functional. The website is also serving as a digital platform for waste sector players.
4.2 One National Training Manual for Sorting Municipal Solid Waste developed and disseminated in collaboration between NEMA and the Ministry of Water and Environment.
4.3 The standardized baselines for computing emission reduction from waste and wastewater is under review by the Climate Change Department under Ministry of Water and Environment pending final review by an international firm.
4.4 The NAMA is registered on the UNFCCC website.
